title: Responsive Article Page Layout
description: Code a full article page layout that adapts from single column to two‑column with a sidebar, using mobile‑first CSS Grid.
problemStatement:
Build a responsive article page with a header, main article, sidebar, and footer. On mobile, everything stacks in one column. On tablet and up (≥768px), the main article and sidebar appear side by side (article ~70%, sidebar ~30%). **HTML:** ```html
My Blog

Article Title

Article content...

About Me

Sidebar content...

© 2025
``` **CSS:** - Global box‑sizing reset. - Mobile‑first: `.content` is a single column (just block). - At `min-width: 768px`, make `.content` a grid with `grid-template-columns: 2fr 1fr;` and a gap of 2rem. - The header and footer should span full width and have background colours, padding. - Ensure the sidebar doesn't get too wide; maybe give it a max‑width or rely on grid fractions. - Use `min-height: 100vh` on body and a sticky footer trick if you like: make body a flex column, main flex:1, but not strictly required. - Add some basic typography (font family, line heights). Write full HTML with internal CSS. Include the viewport meta tag.
hints: Use `grid-template-columns: 1fr;` for mobile, but you can also just rely on block flow; switching to `display: grid` at the breakpoint is fine.
To prevent the sidebar from stretching too wide on ultra‑wide screens, you might want to add a `max-width` to the whole page and centre it.
Remember to test that the sidebar goes below the article on mobile, as per source order (article first, then aside).
expectedOutput: A responsive page where mobile shows article above sidebar, and desktop shows them side by side with proportional widths.
